status: Literature review and design recommendations only. No new detector, provider calls, generated subject tests, or benchmark executions.
user_request: Read the accepted Testora and RippleGUItester papers, assess what to learn, and explain the scope of their LLM use for our coding-agent issue-resolution test augmentation research.
scope: Two user-selected papers, with official artifacts and selected published logs. This is not an exhaustive related-work or novelty search.

method.root_work: Read formal PDFs and relevant current local design and case reviews; inspect key paper tables and figures; synthesize independent notes and verify claim boundaries.

testora_artifact.snapshot_limit: Consistent with released experiment configuration; logs do not identify the precise source commit of every run.
testora_artifact.current_main_limit: Newer default model and prompts are not the published paper configuration.

ripple_paper.version_limit: Use formal paper status counts, not the earlier 20-page arXiv version or stale conference abstract.

ripple_artifact.note: This is the repository linked in the formal paper's Data Availability section. An older public repository is distinct.

research_questions.question: What is the focused software-engineering insight?
research_questions.testora: An observed behavioral difference needs interpretation against development intent; generation and semantic oracle are separate.
research_questions.ripple: Changed code can affect other user scenarios; source history and real historical bug scenarios guide the expansion of intent-based testing.
research_questions.transfer: Agent validation history may expose the conditions under which a patch was checked. Search a relevant legal context outside those checks and verify its actual construction.
research_questions.status_of_transfer: Design hypothesis, not an established effect.

research_questions.question: Where do the papers use LLMs?
research_questions.testora: Usage-program generation; repair based on statically found undefined references; intent-based difference classification; historical artifact also selects expected old/new behavior. Deterministic execution, stability checking and reduction do not form an LLM test-search feedback loop.
research_questions.ripple: Change-impact reasoning, scenario generation and expansion, concrete data instantiation, screenshot-based action selection, visual bug judgment and filtering. Program tools supply git history links, retrieval, action execution/replay and pixel differences.
research_questions.transfer: LLMs can select hypotheses and analysis questions before final judgment. A complete formal model or exhaustive static candidate list need not be an entry requirement.

research_questions.question: What do the results establish?
research_questions.answer: Real-project bug-finding feasibility and substantial oracle/search limits. Neither paper establishes every component's independent gain with equal-budget ablations. Their results do not establish our augmentation effectiveness or issue-resolution improvement.

claim_ledger.claim: Default Testora multi-question classifier precision is 55%, recall 67% on already-observed differences, not all regressions.
claim_ledger.support: Formal paper Table 5, pp.6 and 9; published logs independently recounted by two readers.
claim_ledger.caution: Single/multi logs differ in one ground-truth label; reproduce reported metrics separately without silently changing them.

claim_ledger.claim: Testora found differences in 100 of 525 checked PRs; 82 PRs with no available generated tests were among excluded PRs.
claim_ledger.support: Formal paper Tables 3-4 and released logs.
claim_ledger.caution: 100 differences are not 100 defects. The 19 regression discoveries come from a separate multi-round activity, not an interchangeable 525-PR denominator.

claim_ledger.claim: Ripple evaluated 111 PRs; 146 TP and 173 FP reports give 45.8% precision. 117 is a different deduplicated discovery count.
claim_ledger.support: Formal paper Table 1, p.13; official metric script.
claim_ledger.caution: The detector and metric include some pre-existing issues. Not all accepted reports establish newly introduced regressions.

claim_ledger.claim: Ripple matched 13 of 46 usable known Firefox targets, or 28.3%, leaving 33 misses.
claim_ledger.support: Formal paper Section 4.4 and Figure 8, pp.15-16.
claim_ledger.caution: 41 includes additional unique true positives and is not the known-target recall numerator.

claim_ledger.claim: Separate sorting and new-login scenarios missed creating and saving a login while Username sorting is active.
claim_ledger.support: Formal paper p.16, discussion of Issue 1725969.
claim_ledger.transfer: Scenario diversity does not imply that critical state and action coexist in one execution.
claim_ledger.limit: This motivates our question; it does not establish our implementation's success.

claim_ledger.claim: The formal paper's 26 submitted reports consist of 18 fixed, 3 confirmed and 5 intended.
claim_ledger.caution: A paper-time status snapshot, not current status recount. Do not call all 26 confirmed bugs.

claim_ledger.claim: A strict base/final difference requirement can miss an incomplete fix whose behavior remains wrong in both versions.
claim_ledger.support: Testora Section 2.5 describes skipping equal outputs; logical transfer to issue resolution.
claim_ledger.caution: Do not generalize this hard gate to Ripple. Its detector prompt permits all bugs and results include pre-existing issues.

claim_ledger.claim: Accepted papers with real findings do not by themselves prove that history retrieval, prompt decomposition or a specific component caused the gains.
claim_ledger.support: Full evaluation sections: Testora has classifier prompt/model comparison but no complete generator baseline; Ripple lacks equal-budget method baselines and component ablations.

local_comparison.status: Existing source-pair equality search is a design specification, not a newly evaluated detector.

cases.T13: Two distinct closures sharing a capture cell must remain shared across transfer. Two references to the same function are a different structure.
cases.T17: An existing element whose value is undefined must remain distinct from an absent element when applying defaults.
cases.T24: The same schema and violating input should be checked through the default-mode entry. This constraint is visible in final tests, so it does not alone demonstrate unique trajectory value.
cases.T28: Explicit trajectory assumptions about hash normalization order and replacement of a mount path can guide source and execution checks.
cases.T08: A wrong existing expected result is an oracle issue, not automatically a missing input combination.

keep: Reuse of the original test's working setup
Independent public-contract support for final assertions
Separation of search progress, valid augmentation and defect detection
recommended_reconsideration.change_to_test: Allow a concrete untested context to be proposed before requiring two source locations and an equality relation. Use pair relations as one focused check when appropriate.
recommended_reconsideration.why: Missing operations, state continuity, observations and embedded-language semantics may not have a natural pair representation at proposal time. This is a possible design restriction, not a proven cause of all previous misses.
recommended_reconsideration.counterargument: Broader hypotheses can become vague and reduce verifiability. Retain a concrete original validation, legal context, intended operation and observable result. Measure exclusions and runtime condition fidelity before choosing the design.
recommended_reconsideration.consensus_strength: All three independent readers support this as a testable direction. None claims it is already superior.

next_pilot_questions_not_executed: At a fixed task set, which valid targets does mandatory source-pair equality exclude, compared with concrete-context proposals?

With the same code, tests, model and budget, does source-linked trajectory history improve valid targets beyond final-test evidence? Use irrelevant matched history as an additional control where useful.
For the same target and seed test at equal total budget, does condition-specific execution feedback improve actual condition construction and contract-supported defect detection?
boundaries: No claim of zero false positives from either paper.
Agent reasoning is diagnostic evidence, not normative correctness authority.
Gold patches and benchmark failure tests remain offline evaluation evidence.
No inference from a generated witness to improved resolution rate.
No novelty dismissal based solely on shared LLM, retrieval, differential testing or program-analysis components.
No current algorithm or statistics were changed during this literature review.
